page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8124M cores running at 3.4 GHz. The instance is equipped with 10.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.62 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside weaker multi-core and memory performance. The single-core Geekbench score of 1133.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1406.1 place it in the average tier. However, multi-core metrics show limitations, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2509.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 4360.55, both categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large block read-only bandwidth at 25.89 GB/sec and a Passmark memory score of 1031.78, which is rated as poor.

The c5n.xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile suitable for network-bound workloads that require moderate single-threaded CPU performance but do not demand high memory throughput or local storage. While it supports advanced instruction sets like AVX and AVX-512F, its overall resource density and weak multi-threaded performance represent a tradeoff for parallel processing tasks. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale network-optimized utility workloads rather than memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded compilation.
